# Code 

## Including Code and Code Snippets

Quarto supports executable code, code examples, and syntax-highlighted snippets for a wide range of programming languages. This makes it ideal for creating teaching materials, laboratory manuals, lecture notes, and technical documentation.

To show code as an example without executing it, set `#| eval: false`.

    `````markdown 


    ::: {#ade903ad .cell execution_count=1}
    ``` {.python .cell-code}
    import numpy as np
    x = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
    ```
    :::
    
    
    `````

::: {#7e5541e5 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import numpy as np
x = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
```
:::


### Running Code

Executable code is placed inside a code chunk. Without the `#| eval: false` the code will run.

```text

::: {#0309ebf6 .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
print("Hello, world!")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
Hello, world!
```
:::
:::


```

::: {#3c514079 .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
print("Hello, world!")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
Hello, world!
```
:::
:::


## Showing Output but Hiding Code
You can run the code and display the output  but hide the code source from viewers with `#| echo: false`

````text

::: {#a390bee2 .cell execution_count=5}

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
Only the output will appear.

## Folding Long Code Blocks

Long code examples can be collapsed to avoid cluttering the document.

::: {#71c4700c .cell execution_count=7}
``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Show Python code"}
print("This code is initially hidden.")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
This code is initially hidden.
```
:::
:::


::: {.callout-note}

The folding code blocks are expanded in the static PDF output.

:::

## Figures from code {#sec-codefigs}

Figures generated from Python, R, or Julia code are **automatically** treated as figures. You can include the following (this generates a plot output and echos the original commands)

::: {#cell-fig-line-plot .cell execution_count=8}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.plot([1, 23, 2, 4])
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![A simple line plot](code_files/figure-html/fig-line-plot-output-1.png){#fig-line-plot width=566 height=411 fig-alt='Line graph showing values increasing and decreasing across four observations.'}
:::
:::


::: {.callout}

Often it's useful to add  `#| echo: false` at the start of the figure will make sure to not echo the code and only display the figure:

::: {#cell-fig-line-plot-noecho .cell execution_count=9}

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![A simple line plot](code_files/figure-html/fig-line-plot-noecho-output-1.png){#fig-line-plot-noecho width=566 height=411 fig-alt='A simplified plot with the `#| echo: false` to not show the code'}
:::
:::


:::



## Global Code Options

Chunk options can be applied to every code block using the document YAML.

````markdown
---
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---
````
